answer.summary: Kubernetes High Availability combines **TopologySpreadConstraints** (spatial spreading across AZs and Nodes) with **PodDisruptionBudget (PDB)** (temporal protection against node drains and platform upgrades) to guarantee zero downtime.
reasons: TopologySpreadConstraints distributes pods evenly across AWS AZs and Nodes with maxSkew: 1.
PDB mathematically enforces a minimum percentage of pods (e.g. minAvailable: 40%) during voluntary evictions.
kubectl drain commands that would breach the minimum available budget are strictly blocked by the API server.
answer.scope: Evaluated on AWS EKS v1.35 with multi-AZ SPOT node groups across us-east-1a and us-east-1b.

items.detail: Operator or CI/CD runs kubectl drain NODE_NAME --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data.
Eviction API validates that remaining running pods satisfy minAvailable threshold.
Kube-scheduler provisions replacement pods onto remaining healthy nodes per TopologySpreadConstraints.
Node upgrades complete and operator runs kubectl uncordon NODE_NAME to restore scheduling.

items: Always pair TopologySpreadConstraints (zone and hostname) with PDB to avoid clustering before draining.
Use DoNotSchedule for strict production multi-AZ separation, or ScheduleAnyway for burst elasticity.
Formula for minAvailable: (Total Pods - Max Pods on Single Node) / Total Pods.
PDB guards against voluntary maintenance (cordon/drain/autoscaling), not sudden hardware failure.
